tables.name: departments
tables.description: One row per academic department of the university.

columns.name: dept_id
columns.doc: Identifier of the department.

columns.name: dept_name
columns.doc: Official name of the department.

columns.name: building
columns.doc: Building that houses the department office.

columns.name: annual_budget
columns.doc: Yearly operating budget of the department, expressed in thousands of euros.

tables.name: instructors
tables.description: One row per member of the teaching staff.

columns.name: instructor_id
columns.doc: Identifier of the instructor.

columns.name: instructor_name
columns.doc: Full name of the instructor.

columns.name: dept_id
columns.doc: Department the instructor belongs to.

columns.name: contract_type
columns.doc: Employment arrangement code: 1 = permanent post, 2 = fixed-term contract, 3 = adjunct paid per course, 4 = visiting lecturer from another university.

columns.name: hire_year
columns.doc: Calendar year in which the instructor was first hired.

tables.name: students
tables.description: One row per student currently registered at the university.

columns.name: student_id
columns.doc: Identifier of the student.

columns.name: student_name
columns.doc: Full name of the student.

columns.name: dept_id
columns.doc: Department of the student's declared major.

columns.name: start_year
columns.doc: Calendar year in which the student first enrolled at the university.

columns.name: fee_category
columns.doc: Fee arrangement code: 1 = standard domestic fee, 2 = international fee, 3 = full scholarship with tuition waived, 4 = staff-dependent discount.

columns.name: account_balance
columns.doc: Current balance of the student's fee account in euros, calculated as payments received minus fees charged, so a negative balance means the student still owes the university.

tables.name: courses
tables.description: One row per course in the catalogue, each taught by a single instructor.

columns.name: course_id
columns.doc: Identifier of the course.

columns.name: course_title
columns.doc: Title of the course as shown in the catalogue.

columns.name: dept_id
columns.doc: Department that offers the course.

columns.name: instructor_id
columns.doc: Instructor who teaches the course.

columns.name: credit_points
columns.doc: Credit value of the course in ECTS points, where one point stands for 26 hours of total student work.

tables.name: enrolments
tables.description: One row per student registration on a course in a given term, with the final grade.

columns.name: enrolment_id
columns.doc: Identifier of the course registration.

columns.name: student_id
columns.doc: Student who registered for the course.

columns.name: course_id
columns.doc: Course the student registered for.

columns.name: term
columns.doc: Term code made of the last two digits of the calendar year in which the academic year starts followed by one semester digit (1 = autumn, 2 = spring, 3 = summer session), so 241 is autumn 2024 and 243 is the summer session of 2025.

columns.name: grade
columns.doc: Final grade on a 1 to 5 scale where 1 is the best, 4 is the lowest passing grade and 5 means the course was failed.

tables.name: fee_payments
tables.description: One row per payment received from a student by the bursar's office.

columns.name: payment_id
columns.doc: Identifier of the payment.

columns.name: student_id
columns.doc: Student who made the payment.

columns.name: amount
columns.doc: Amount paid, in euros.

columns.name: kind
columns.doc: Payment purpose code: 1 = tuition instalment, 2 = late-payment penalty, 3 = exam resit fee, 4 = refundable equipment deposit.

columns.name: paid_on
columns.doc: Date the payment was received, written as DD/MM/YYYY.

questions.text: Give me the number of visiting lecturers on our staff.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM instructors WHERE contract_type = 4

needs_docs.fact: code 4 means a visiting lecturer from another university

questions.text: Name the students who study on a full scholarship.
questions.sql: SELECT student_name FROM students WHERE fee_category = 3 ORDER BY student_name

needs_docs.fact: code 3 means a full scholarship with tuition waived

questions.text: Which course has handed out the most top marks?
questions.sql: SELECT c.course_title FROM enrolments e JOIN courses c ON c.course_id = e.course_id WHERE e.grade = 1 GROUP BY c.course_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, c.course_title LIMIT 1

needs_docs.fact: grades run from 1 to 5 and 1 is the best grade, 5 is a fail

questions.text: Count the course registrations we had in the summer of 2025.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM enrolments WHERE term = '243'

needs_docs.fact: the first two digits of a term code give the year the academic year starts and the last digit the semester, so the summer session of 2025 is code 243

questions.text: For the Databases course, what is the total student workload in hours?
questions.sql: SELECT credit_points * 26 FROM courses WHERE course_title = 'Databases'

needs_docs.fact: one credit point stands for 26 hours of total student work

questions.text: How many students currently owe the university money?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM students WHERE account_balance < 0

needs_docs.fact: the balance is payments minus fees charged, so a negative balance means the student owes money

questions.text: How much have we collected so far in late-payment penalties?
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM fee_payments WHERE kind = 2

questions.text: During March 2025, how much money came in from student payments?
questions.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) FROM fee_payments WHERE SUBSTR(paid_on, 4, 7) = '03/2025'

needs_docs.fact: dates are written day/month/year, so the middle part is the month

questions.sql: SELECT i.instructor_name FROM courses c JOIN instructors i ON i.instructor_id = c.instructor_id WHERE c.course_title = 'Linear Algebra'

questions.text: I'd like to know how many courses the Computer Science department runs.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM courses c JOIN departments d ON d.dept_id = c.dept_id WHERE d.dept_name = 'Computer Science'

readings.sql: SELECT d.dept_name FROM departments d JOIN students s ON s.dept_id = d.dept_id GROUP BY d.dept_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, d.dept_name LIMIT 1
SELECT dept_name FROM departments ORDER BY annual_budget DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Department size is conventionally measured by the number of students majoring in it.

ambiguous.text: Which instructor has the heaviest teaching load?

readings.sql: SELECT i.instructor_name FROM instructors i JOIN courses c ON c.instructor_id = i.instructor_id GROUP BY i.instructor_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, i.instructor_name LIMIT 1

readings.gloss: has the most student registrations across their courses
readings.sql: SELECT i.instructor_name FROM instructors i JOIN courses c ON c.instructor_id = i.instructor_id JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY i.instructor_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, i.instructor_name LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Teaching load is counted as the number of courses an instructor teaches.

ambiguous.text: Which student is our top payer?

readings.gloss: highest total paid across all payments
readings.sql: SELECT s.student_name FROM students s JOIN fee_payments p ON p.student_id = s.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id ORDER BY SUM(p.amount) DESC, s.student_name LIMIT 1
SELECT s.student_name FROM students s JOIN fee_payments p ON p.student_id = s.student_id GROUP BY s.student_id ORDER BY MAX(p.amount) DESC, s.student_name LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: The top payer is taken to be the student whose payments add up to the highest total.

readings.sql: SELECT c.course_title FROM courses c JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.course_id GROUP BY c.course_id ORDER BY AVG(e.grade) DESC, c.course_title LIMIT 1
SELECT c.course_title FROM courses c JOIN enrolments e ON e.course_id = c.course_id WHERE e.grade = 5 GROUP BY c.course_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, c.course_title LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Course difficulty is judged by the average grade of its students, a weaker average meaning a tougher course.

readings.gloss: started in the latest start year only
readings.sql: SELECT student_name FROM students WHERE start_year = (SELECT MAX(start_year) FROM students) ORDER BY student_name

readings.gloss: started in the latest two start years
readings.sql: SELECT student_name FROM students WHERE start_year >= (SELECT MAX(start_year) FROM students) - 1 ORDER BY student_name

resolving_note.text: Recent joiners are the students who started in the latest start year on record.
